_note: BIOLOGY ONLY. Compiled from general spearfishing-guide sources (not a validated regional survey), for Oahu's tropical Central Pacific reef fauna. Depth, temperature, substrate and season of presence and how each species responds to water clarity. None of it is law - Hawaii has its own size/bag rules and some species (notably large terminal-phase uhu) are subject to conservation guidance that is not encoded anywhere in this app.

species.note: Uhu - grazes algae on shallow lava reef, easy to locate but quick to duck into coral when spooked. Large blue terminal-phase males are the breeders that keep the population healthy; many local spearos let the biggest ones swim.
Kumu - the most prized eating fish in Hawaii. Works sandy patches and rubble adjacent to reef rather than the reef itself, and typically sits deeper than beginner divers are comfortable with.
Omilu - hunts sandy patches adjacent to reef structure, often in pairs or small groups. Less wary than giant trevally and a common intermediate target.
Ulua - the headline gamefish here, patrolling reef edges and channel drop-offs. Powerful and wary; ambush from cover down-current rather than chase.

Roi - introduced to Hawaii and now invasive, actively encouraged to harvest since it competes with and preys on native reef fish. Large individuals carry a real ciguatera risk, so check size before eating one.
Mu - one of the more wary and challenging reef fish to approach here, holding near structure edges over sand.

_legal_note: Legal rules live in legal/<JURISDICTION>.json and are merged in at run time. No legal pack exists yet for US-HI, so this app will correctly show 'not researched' rather than any size or season claim - Hawaii DLNR publishes the real rules, including size limits on several of the species above.
